key_insight: FurnitureVLA shows that vision-language-action models can be extended from toy tasks to real-scale, long-horizon bimanual furniture assembly. The paper’s core breakthrough is a full pipeline for training and evaluating robots on complex assembly with both simulation and real-world human demonstrations.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between simple robot manipulation benchmarks and the messy, multi-step reality of assembling full-size furniture. It tackles long-horizon coordination, bimanual control, and scalable data collection for real-world assembly tasks.
method: Formulates real-scale bimanual furniture assembly as a structured VLA task.
Builds a scalable simulation pipeline to generate expert trajectories and evaluate assembly policies.
Develops a VR teleoperation system that lets one operator control both robot arms to collect high-quality demonstrations.
impact: This work provides a practical blueprint for training robots on complex household assembly tasks that require planning, coordination, and two-handed manipulation. For ML practitioners, it expands the frontier of embodied AI beyond simplified lab setups and offers reusable infrastructure for long-horizon robot learning.

paper_title: FurnitureVLA: Learning Long-Horizon Bimanual Furniture Assembly with Vision-Language-Action Model
paper_authors: Chenyang Ma, Yue Yang, Radu Corcodel, Siddarth Jain, Andrew Wu
